hook: Tom Mitchell helped establish machine learning as an academic discipline in its own right. He earned a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from MIT in 1973 and a PhD from Stanford University in 1979, studying under Bruce Buchanan. After teaching at Rutgers University, he joined Carnegie Mellon University in 1986, where he became the E. Fredkin Professor and later the founding chair of the world's first Machine Learning Department in 2006. In 1997 he published the textbook Machine Learning, one of the first comprehensive textbooks in the field and still used in university courses. His later research pushed machine learning into new territory, including the Never-Ending Language Learner project, which continuously extracts facts from web text, and work using brain imaging to study how the brain represents word meaning. He has also studied the effects of AI on the labor market, co-chairing a National Academies report on AI and the future of work.

quick_facts: Founding chair of Carnegie Mellon University's Machine Learning Department, the first freestanding department of its kind, established in 2006
Author of the textbook Machine Learning (McGraw Hill, 1997), one of the first comprehensive textbooks in the field
Leads the Never-Ending Language Learner (NELL) project, which has continuously extracted facts from web text since January 2010
Uses brain imaging to study how the human brain represents the meaning of words and sentences
Elected to the National Academy of Engineering in 2010
Co-chaired the National Academies report AI and the Future of Work, published in November 2024

achievements.title: Founding Chair, Machine Learning Department, Carnegie Mellon University
achievements.impact: Established the first freestanding academic department dedicated to machine learning, helping formalize the field as a distinct discipline.

achievements.title: Machine Learning textbook (1997)
achievements.impact: Wrote one of the first comprehensive textbooks on machine learning, used for decades to train new generations of researchers and practitioners.

achievements.title: Never-Ending Language Learner (NELL)
achievements.impact: Built a system that has continuously read the web and extracted structured facts since 2010, demonstrating long running, self improving machine learning in practice.

achievements.title: Brain imaging research on language meaning
achievements.impact: Applied machine learning to fMRI data to study how the brain encodes word and sentence meaning, connecting AI methods to cognitive neuroscience.
